scene: Two children run a makeshift stall selling tinned food from a wooden table in a tent camp, laundry strung overhead and a younger girl running past behind them.
framing_direction: STEP BACK and SHOOT vertical so the washing line and camp tents fill the top half; PLACE the children and their table in the lower half; WAIT for the girl's eyes to lift toward you; KEEP the running child in the background for movement.
why_it_works: Children doing adult work to survive tells the story of loss without any graphic content; the domestic details (laundry, tins) make it relatable and the girl's direct, serious gaze stops the scroll.
creator: Jaber Jehad Badwan

scene: A boy laughs straight into the camera as water pours over his head during UNRWA summer games.
framing_direction: GET IN CLOSE and FILL the vertical frame with the face; KEEP the eyes about a third of the way down; SHOOT a burst while the water hits and he laughs; USE the bright background for colour contrast.
why_it_works: Pure joy with direct eye contact is an instant scroll-stopper and gives donors hope: a reminder that these are children who deserve a childhood. Use it as the 'hope' counterpart to need shots.
creator: United Nations Photo

scene: A family is displaced on the back of an overloaded vehicle piled with buckets, jerry cans and mattresses, passing destroyed buildings; a child peers out from between the belongings.
framing_direction: FOLLOW the vehicle from behind at walking pace; FRAME it tall, with the belongings stacked up the frame; FIND the child's face peeking out and FOCUS on it; LET the ruined street lead away into the distance.
why_it_works: Everything a family owns on one cart reads instantly as 'they have lost their home'; the small face among the possessions makes it personal and urgent.
creator: Jaber Jehad Badwan
